draft.title: Amortisation tables
card: An amortisation table lists a loan period by period. Its columns are the payment, the interest, the reduction in principal and the balance.
Interest = balance at the start of the period × the interest rate for that period. Reduction in principal = payment − interest.
New balance = old balance − reduction in principal. The interest is not taken off the balance, because it is the cost of borrowing.

Example: a $10 000 loan has interest of 6% per year, charged yearly, with a payment of $2000. Interest = 10 000 × 0.06 = $600. Reduction in principal = 2000 − 600 = $1400. New balance = 10 000 − 1400 = $8600.
draft.remember: Interest comes from the starting balance. Only the rest of the payment cuts the balance.

a.q: A loan balance is $5000 and the interest rate is 4% per period. The payment is $1000. What is the reduction in principal for this period?
a.why: Interest = 5000 × 0.04 = $200. Reduction in principal = 1000 − 200 = $800. The $200 is the interest, so it is not the amount that reduces the principal.
a.clue: Find the interest first, then take it from the payment.

b.q: Priya has a loan with a balance of $8000. The interest is 3% per period and the payment is $1500. What is the balance after this payment?
b.why: Interest = 8000 × 0.03 = $240. Reduction in principal = 1500 − 240 = $1260. New balance = 8000 − 1260 = $6740. $6500 is wrong because it takes the whole payment off and ignores the interest.
b.clue: Only the part of the payment left after interest reduces the balance.

problems.detail: "The interest is not taken off the balance, because it is the cost of borrowing" is muddled. In fact the interest is added to the balance and the whole payment is taken off, which gives the same result as old balance − reduction in principal. The sentence could leave students thinking interest never affects the balance, and the reason given does not explain why.

check.summary: Both answers check out ($800 and $6740), and the distractors and explanations are sound. One card sentence, about interest not being taken off the balance, is confusing and should be reworded to say interest is added and the payment subtracted.

proposal.title: Amortisation tables
card: An amortisation table lists a loan period by period. Its columns are the payment, the interest, the reduction in principal and the balance.
Interest = balance at the start of the period × the interest rate for that period. Reduction in principal = payment − interest.
Each period the interest is added to the balance and the whole payment is taken off. So new balance = old balance + interest − payment, which equals old balance − reduction in principal.

Example: a $10 000 loan has interest of 6% per year, charged yearly, with a payment of $2000. Interest = 10 000 × 0.06 = $600. Reduction in principal = 2000 − 600 = $1400. New balance = 10 000 + 600 − 2000 = $8600.
proposal.remember: Part of each payment covers the interest. Only what is left over cuts the balance.

a.q: A loan balance is $5000 and the interest rate is 4% per period. The payment is $1000. What is the reduction in principal for this period?
a.why: Interest = 5000 × 0.04 = $200. Reduction in principal = 1000 − 200 = $800. The $200 is the interest, which the payment must cover first, so it is not the amount that reduces the principal.
a.clue: Find the interest first, then take it from the payment.

b.q: Priya has a loan with a balance of $8000. The interest is 3% per period and the payment is $1500. What is the balance after this payment?
b.why: Interest = 8000 × 0.03 = $240. New balance = 8000 + 240 − 1500 = $6740, the same as 8000 − 1260. $6500 is wrong because it ignores the interest added to the balance, and $6260 takes the interest off instead of adding it.
b.clue: Interest is added to the balance before the payment comes off.

final.title: Amortisation tables
card: An amortisation table lists a loan period by period. Its columns are the payment, the interest, the reduction in principal and the balance.
Interest \(=\) balance at the start of the period \(\times\) the interest rate for that period. Reduction in principal \(=\) payment \(-\) interest.

Each period the interest is added to the balance and the whole payment is taken off. So new balance \(=\) old balance \(+\) interest \(-\) payment, which equals old balance \(-\) reduction in principal.

Example: a $10,000 loan has interest of 6% per year, charged yearly, with a payment of $2000. Interest \(= \$10{,}000 \times 0.06 = \$600\). Reduction in principal \(= \$2000 - \$600 = \$1400\). New balance \(= \$10{,}000 + \$600 - \$2000\), which is $8600.
final.remember: Part of each payment covers the interest. Only what is left over cuts the balance.

a.why: Interest \(= \$5000 \times 0.04 = \$200\). Reduction in principal \(= \$1000 - \$200 = \$800\). The $200 is the interest, which the payment must cover first, so it is not the amount that reduces the principal.
a.clue: Find the interest first, then take it from the payment.

b.q: Priya has a loan with a balance of $8000. The interest is 3% per period and the payment is $1500. What is the balance after this payment?
b.why: Interest \(= \$8000 \times 0.03 = \$240\). New balance \(= \$8000 + \$240 - \$1500\), which is $6740, the same as \(\$8000 - \$1260\). $6500 is wrong because it ignores the interest added to the balance, and $6260 takes the interest off instead of adding it.
